title: Resolve the mirrored role data-scope model without changing the permission tables
goal: role_service.go declares its own copy of the role data-scope policy model with a comment saying it mirrors another directory's model to avoid a cross-directory import, and the delete path writes both tables. That is a deliberate duplication, but deliberate duplication still drifts. This wave is an investigation-first task: diff the two model definitions against the live schema, prove whether they are still identical, and then either move the model to a shared home and delete the mirror, or record that the mirror must stay and add a checker that fails when the two definitions diverge. No table, migration, policy behaviour or permission result changes in this wave.
findings: RC-022 (P2): role_service.go:65-78 declares a model that mirrors another directory's role data-scope policy model, with an explicit comment about avoiding a cross-directory import; the delete path writes both tables at role_service.go:614-628.
Drift risk: two definitions of one table mean a future column addition can land in one and not the other, and no checker compares them.

in: Diff the two model definitions against the live schema and record every difference
If identical: move the model to a shared location both packages may import and delete the mirror
If not identical: record which definition is authoritative and why the mirror exists, then add a mechanical checker that fails on divergence
Keep the delete path writing the same tables it writes today
out: Creating, dropping or altering any table
Changing data-scope resolution or permission results
Moving the table between packages as a schema change

implementationNotes: Start with the diff, not the refactor. If the models already differ, the finding is a latent defect rather than duplication and the wave's output is the drift report plus a checker.

The cross-directory import that the comment avoids may exist for a real layering reason. If moving the model would create a package cycle, keep the mirror and add the checker instead; a cycle is worse than a duplicate.
Do not touch the migration set. The two definitions describe existing tables, and this wave changes no DDL.
The checker belongs with the existing scripts/harness/check-* family and must be added to the npm script list and CI only if the maintainer approves a new gate.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Investigate before changing anything; the default outcome may be 'keep the mirror and add a checker'.
reviewerPosture: Check the drift report compares every column and tag, not just the struct name.
Check no migration or DDL changed.
Check data-scope results are unchanged for all five modes.
Check any new checker is deterministic and does not need a database.

runtimeEvidence: data-scope resolution result for all five modes before and after
schema dump of the role data-scope table compared with both model definitions

humanGates: Approve moving the model or keeping the mirror plus a checker.
Approve adding a new mechanical checker to the gate set if one is proposed.
completionChecklist: Model drift report exists and compares every field
Decision recorded: shared model or mirror plus divergence checker
No schema, migration or data-scope behaviour changed
